title: MAIDEN BEAD: fort data readers + 'fortkit status' CLI
description: Library + CLI reading ~/.claude/civilization.json, then per fort: .beads/issues.jsonl (passive export — read-only, never source of truth), fort/events/*.jsonl, fort/handoffs/, git state (ahead/behind, worktrees). Output: JSON summary per fort + a human table — the world view as text before pixels. Node/TS, fixture-fort tests, self-verifying. Supervised maiden run.
design:
SPEC (Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04, dispatch approved by Overseer; supervised maiden run — Overseer present).

WHAT: a library (src/) + CLI entry 'fortkit status' built on the gzn scaffold (strict tsc, Biome, vitest — verify.sh is the gate). The world view as text before pixels.

READERS (library, one module per source):
1. Registry: ~/.claude/civilization.json — the fort list; tolerate missing/partial entries (a fort dir may not exist on this machine).
2. Beads: <fort>/.beads/issues.jsonl — PASSIVE EXPORT, read-only, never source of truth; parse defensively (skip+count malformed lines, never throw on one bad record). Do not shell out to bd.
3. Events: <fort>/fort/events/events-*.jsonl — schema per schema/events.md (vendored copy is law here). TIME BASIS (fortkit-dpu decision, verbatim law): group by PARSED UTC instant, NEVER by filename; the day-file name is a shard key, not a fact.
4. Handoffs: <fort>/fort/handoffs/*.md — filename gives seat+date; title line only, no prose parsing.
5. Git: ahead/behind of upstream (absent remote => nulls, not errors), worktree list, dirty flag. Plain 'git -C' subprocess is fine; no libgit dep.

OUTPUT: per-fort JSON summary (machine) + human table (--json flag switches; table is default). Summary fields: fort name, path, open/in_progress/blocked/closed bead counts, last event ts (UTC) + actor, last handoff (seat, date), git state. Missing sources render as absent, not as crashes.

TESTS (replace gzn's placeholder test): fixture fort(s) under test fixtures — synthetic civilization.json, issues.jsonl, events files, handoffs; no dependence on the real ~/.claude or this live fort. REQUIRED (dpu): an event written at 2026-08-03T23:24-08:00 groups into the same UTC day as a bead created 2026-08-04T07:23Z. Also required: malformed-line tolerance test; missing-fort-dir test.

BOUNDARIES: read-only over all fort data — the tool never writes beads, events, or git. Do not modify fort/scripts/status.sh (shell status is the fort's own; this is the product CLI). Node LTS per engines pin; no new runtime deps without flagging in the report.
notes:
WARDEN VERDICT, ROUND 1 (recorded verbatim by Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04):

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass, Opus): VERDICT: request-changes

Reviewed: bead `fortkit-jmq`, commit `0807f41` on `bead/jmq`, worktree `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/jmq`. Author: Kethra Anvilmark (Forge), model gpt-5.6-terra. Judged against the bead's DESIGN spec, the Manyhalls charter standing orders, and the Overseer's bar.

The implementation itself is competent. The readers are small, typed, defensively written, and the required dpu pinning test is real rather than decorative. Two findings block, and both concern the dependency change rather than the product code.

1. BLOCKING. `package.json` declares two devDependencies as tarballs in `/tmp`, and the manifest disagrees with the lockfile. package.json contains "@types/node": "file:../../../../../tmp/types-node-22.19.7.tgz" and "undici-types": "file:../../../../../tmp/undici-types-6.21.0.tgz". Those tarballs exist only as untracked files in /tmp written during the Forge session (14:34/14:36). package-lock.json's root block declares "@types/node": "^22.19.7" as a registry range and does not list undici-types among root devDependencies: manifest and lock disagree on both. Verified by `npm ci --dry-run --offline` on a scratch copy: npm entered an unbounded retry loop on the unresolvable tarballs. Correct fix: ordinary registry ranges, lockfile regenerated from the registry; undici-types dropped entirely (it is a transitive dep of @types/node and the lock already carries it as one). This matters most because fortkit is the settlement factory: a package.json that only installs on this machine, today, before /tmp clears, is the kind of defect that gets copied into forts that do not exist yet.

2. BLOCKING. The handoff's "Verified facts"/"Failed attempts" misdescribe finding 1. fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-04.md claims "the final `npm ci` remains reproducible where registry access is available" — not true: the manifest is not registry-resolved, so npm ci is not reproducible anywhere. The handoff and /tmp/forge-jmq.log both omit the file:/tmp specs and the existence of undici-types. Standing order 7: records are never falsified; no intent alleged (likelier the summary described the intended end state, not the achieved one), but the correction must be APPENDED to the handoff, not edited in.

3. Non-blocking (wants a bead). verify.sh never runs npm ci/install, so a manifest that cannot install passes every gate — which is exactly what happened; re-verified independently (exit 0 against the broken package.json). Follow-up bead: install-integrity step in the verifier, plus standing-order-5 verification bead.

4. Non-blocking, fix before merge. In src/readers/events.ts and handoffs.ts, readdir is guarded but the subsequent readFile is not: a directory-named match, unreadable file, or list/read race rejects through Promise.all in readFortStatus and crashes the CLI. Spec requires missing sources render as absent; event shards are appended concurrently, so the race is real.

5. Non-blocking, fix before merge. src/readers/git.ts runs `git status --porcelain` without --no-optional-locks; git status opportunistically rewrites .git/index (demonstrated in a throwaway repo). readCivilizationStatus reaches into every registered fort and can contend for index.lock mid-commit elsewhere. Adding --no-optional-locks makes the "never writes git" boundary literally true. The other three git calls are genuinely read-only.

6. Non-blocking (decision wanted). The dpu pinning test is genuinely discriminating on the event side (23:24-08:00 vs 07:23Z cross-file ordering; filename-ordered implementations fail it). But beads.ts never parses created_at, so the cross-source half of the requirement is asserted against the string literal "2026-08-04" rather than a day derived from a bead. Decide whether that satisfies the dpu law or whether the day basis becomes a shared function used by both readers.

7. Non-blocking, NEEDS ATTENTION. No fort in the civilization has a .beads/issues.jsonl — checked all three registry entries; not present, not tracked, not gitignored. This beads generation is Dolt-backed and does not produce the passive export. The reader is correct per spec and returns null, so bead counts — the headline of the maiden product — are empty in production everywhere. Drift between spec assumption and installed beads; should have been raised as a question, not absorbed into a null (standing order 2). Needs a bead: configure a JSONL export or point the reader at the real source.

8. Non-blocking. Fixture not hermetic: test/fixtures/fort-alpha sits inside the worktree, so the git reader's four subprocesses run against the live fortkit repo (resolves to the real worktree index). Nothing asserted on the result today, but npm test reaches out of its fixtures, and combined with 5 that is where the latent index write would fire. Also: no test covers the git reader or formatStatusTable.

9. Non-blocking nit. beads.ts increments the same `malformed` counter for JSON.parse failures and for well-formed records with unrecognized status — vocabulary drift would masquerade as corruption. Two counters or a distinct unknownStatus.

10. Non-blocking. allowImportingTsExtensions is legitimate (paired with noEmit; enables Node 24 native type stripping). Consistency: src/ imports use .ts extensions while tests import ../src/*.js paths that do not exist on disk and work only via vitest resolution — one convention per repo. `"bin": {"fortkit": "./src/cli.ts"}` (TS source as executable) works under the engines pin but deserves a README line.

11. Non-blocking. Human table omits ahead/behind and closed counts (present in --json); worth a look when bead columns carry data.

Clean, on the record: fort/scripts/status.sh untouched; beads read directly, never shelled to bd; no runtime deps; placeholder test removed as instructed; types model absence as null consistently; ahead/behind parse correct; execFile arg arrays prevent shell interpolation.

Verified independently: full diff line-by-line against DESIGN; verify.sh --no-emit green in worktree; verify.sh contains no install step; the file: specs, tarball timestamps, and lock divergence; the npm ci retry loop; the git status index-mtime behavior with/without --no-optional-locks; fixture-inside-worktree resolution to the live index; no upstream on bead/jmq; absence of issues.jsonl in all three forts; registry key handling against the real civilization.json.
Taken on faith: Kethra's CLI smoke runs (running them would shell git into all three forts — declined as read-only); the sandbox's claimed registry unreachability (does not change finding 1: an unreachable registry is a reason to stop and report, not to commit a manifest pointing at /tmp); the /tmp tarballs' provenance/integrity (unverified — second reason to regenerate from registry); whether the beads status vocabulary is exactly four values.

To clear: fix 1 and 2 (registry ranges, regenerated lock, undici-types dropped, correction appended to handoff); fold 4 and 5 into the same round. 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 want beads; 7 wants the Overseer's attention before the world view is built on a data source that does not exist.

VERDICT-LINE: request-changes: devDeps point at /tmp tarballs, lock disagrees with manifest, handoff misreports it as reproducible; readers otherwise sound

title: CI from commit one: typecheck + lint + test
description: Greenfield rule: no untrusted-verifier era. tsc, lint, test runner on every push.
design:
SPEC (Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04). Context: repo has no Node project yet; fortkit-jmq mandates Node/TS; NO git remote exists, so hosted CI has nowhere to trigger. Therefore two layers, local one authoritative.

LAYER 1 — local verifier, the fort's definition of 'verifiers green' (charter order 9): fort/scripts/verify.sh
- Single entrypoint, fail-fast, exit 0 = green. Steps in order: (1) typecheck: tsc --noEmit, strict; (2) lint; (3) test; (4) shellcheck over bin/fort-init and fort/scripts/*.sh (the existing shell surface is product code too).
- Emits verify.run at start, then verify.pass or verify.fail (payload names the failing step) via fort/scripts/emit.sh. A --no-emit flag (auto-set when $CI is set) skips emission — hosted runners must never write the event stream.
- From this bead's close onward, no bead closes without a green verify.sh at the candidate commit.

LAYER 2 — hosted CI, ready from first push: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Committed now, dormant until the Overseer creates a remote (gate 3, his action, NOT a blocker here). Triggers: push + PR to main. Runs the same steps (npm ci, then verify.sh --no-emit). Node LTS pinned.

SCAFFOLDING (in this bead — verifiers need a project to verify):
- package.json (private, engines pinned), strict tsconfig.json, lint config, test runner config, one placeholder test that passes so the pipeline is proven end to end (replaced when jmq lands real tests).
- Tooling recommendation: vitest for tests; Biome for lint+format (single fast tool). tsc remains the typechecker (Biome does not typecheck). Forge: verify against current best practice per standing order 1 and flag disagreement rather than silently switching.

DOCS (same session, global CLAUDE rules): fill the Build & Test section of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (both — they are independent files); append to fort/remember.md that verify.sh is now the verifier, superseding the 'no verifiers yet' line (append, never edit, order 7).
acceptance_criteria:
- verify.sh runs typecheck, lint, test, shellcheck fail-fast with correct exit codes; --no-emit works; CI env auto-suppresses emission
- Demonstrated in the worktree (not committed): a type error, a lint error, and a failing test each produce nonzero exit and a verify.fail event naming the step
- .github/workflows/ci.yml present and syntactically valid, running the same steps via verify.sh --no-emit
- verify.sh green at the candidate commit; placeholder test passes
- CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md Build & Test sections updated in the same change; fort/remember.md appended
- Warden review before close (charter order 9 — this bead closes under the regime it creates)
notes: CLOSURE RECORD 2026-08-04: Warden approve round 2 (verified against artifacts), merged to main 0ed63c3, post-merge follow-up b11e6a2 (Warden-pre-cleared .claude-flow exclusion in biome.json + .gitignore, formatter-canonical form). Emission-on verify.pass on main at 11:27:07, all four steps. Charter order 9 satisfied under the regime this bead created. DURABLE CAVEAT (Ilva): biome.json has NO vcs block, so Biome does not read .gitignore — the files.includes exclusions do the entire job and are NOT redundant with .gitignore entries; do not delete them as cleanup. Follow-ups live in: fortkit-8ib (template lint strategy, blocks fd2), fortkit-8cq (Forge sandbox commits), fortkit-6ps (launcher concurrency guard), fortkit-jmq (replaces placeholder test).

title: Reader v2.1: labels omitempty + dependency_count-counts-blocks-only (Warden bzx.1 round-2 findings)

I have what I need. Final review:

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-bzx.6, commit `8a0daff` on `bead/bzx.6`, one commit over `main` (42475bd). Work produced by **GPT-5.6 Codex** as Kethra Anvilmark, per `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`. Round one. Nothing blocking.

The diff does what the bead asked and nothing else: six files, confined to `src/readers/beads.ts`, `src/types.ts`, two fixtures, `test/status.test.ts`, and an appended handoff. No gate-listed surface is touched (no auth, no migration, no public-facing change; `fort/handoffs/` is a seat's own record, not constitution — consistent with every prior merge in this repo), so no mandatory escalation applies.

All six acceptance criteria are met, and I checked each against the code rather than the handoff:

- Golden line with a blocks edge committed and pinned — `test/fixtures/beads-golden.jsonl:3` (fortkit-bzx.2: one `blocks` edge, one `parent-child` edge, `dependency_count:1`), pinned by a new `toMatchObject` on edge order and types at `test/status.test.ts:95-102`.
- Unlabelled real line counts zero schemaGaps — `hasSchemaGap` now gates the labels check on `Object.hasOwn` (`src/readers/beads.ts:199-200`), and the golden test asserts `schemaGaps: 0` where the pre-diff code produced 2. That assertion is the regression pin, and it is a *strengthening* of the old test, which asserted only `{open, ready}`.
- `dependency_count > blocks-edges` triggers gap — `beads.ts:180-185`, pinned by the `truncated-blocks` fixture line.
- No unchecked cast on status — `statuses` is now a total `Record<BeadStatus, CountedStatus>` with an `isBeadStatus` guard using `Object.hasOwn` (correctly immune to `toString`/prototype keys); the `as CountedStatus` is gone and `parseBead` narrows `record.status` so the field assignment typechecks unaided.
- `BeadDependency` fields non-null — `types.ts:53-58`. This corrects a type that was already *lying*: `parseDependency` has required all three to be strings since bzx.1. The now-redundant `dependsOnId !== null` check in `isReady` is correctly dropped.
- One shared edge predicate — `isPrerequisiteEdge` (`beads.ts:158-163`), used by both `isReady` and `hasDependencySchemaGap`.

Two judgment calls I looked at hard and agree with. First, `isPrerequisiteEdge` requires `issueId === beadId`, not merely `type === "blocks"`, so if bd ever emits reverse edges on a line they inflate neither the readiness prerequisites nor the truncation count — correct under the settled blocks-only semantics and safe if bd only ever emits outgoing edges. Second, the `dependenciesOrNull` rewrite from `map`+`every`+cast to an early-return loop removes the second unchecked cast and short-circuits; behaviour is identical.

FINDINGS

1. **(non-blocking) The Warden's own scratch copy strips committed test fixtures, so 4 of 21 tests cannot run in review.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` passes rsync `--exclude '.beads'` unanchored, which matches at any depth and therefore removes `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` along with the fort's real bead database. In my cwd, `readBeads` returns `null` for the fixture fort and four tests fail — every one of them a fixture-availability artifact, not a defect in this diff (the condition predates the bead; it dates from whenever the fixture fort was added). The exclusion's intent is sound (`.beads/hooks` is a host-RCE surface, threat 1: agent accident, and threat 3), so the fix is to anchor the pattern to the repo root rather than drop it. This is an observed failure, not an imagined one, so it clears standing order 11. `fort/scripts/warden.sh` is human-gate 1, so this must go through a bead and Justin's hand — I am not proposing an edit. It degrades the review gate but does not make merging this diff worse than not merging it.

2. **(non-blocking) The loosening from `!==` to `>` is not pinned by any test.** The new `truncated-blocks` fixture (count 2, one prerequisite edge) fails the old predicate too, and the golden bzx.2 line (count 1, one blocks edge) passes both. No fixture exercises `dependency_count < prerequisite-edge count`, which is precisely the case the two predicates disagree on. A future refactor back to `!==` would go green. The handoff does not overclaim here — it says the fixture pins the count-greater-than-blocks condition, which is true — so this is a coverage gap, not a false record. Worth a fixture asserting that a low count is tolerated, or an explicit note that the case is considered unreachable.

3. **(non-blocking) The two empirical rules now live only in the bead and the handoff, not in the code.** `beads.ts:189-190` carries a comment explaining bd's omitted dependency array; the parallel labels-omitempty rule (`beads.ts:145-147`, `199-200`) and the reason `>` was chosen over `!=` have none. These are exactly the facts a stranger porting this reader into a new fort will need, and this file will be copied.

4. **(non-blocking) `typeof record.id === "string"` is evaluated inside the per-edge filter callback** (`beads.ts:183`). It is a loop-invariant that is already guaranteed by `parseBead` having returned non-null before this function is called; hoisting it above the `filter` would read better and make the guarantee visible.

5. **(non-blocking) The new golden line is a partial transcription and a moment-in-time snapshot.** It omits `description`/`acceptance_criteria`, which its neighbouring real line (fortkit-bzx.5) carries; and since fortkit-bzx.6 itself blocks fortkit-bzx.2, the live line today most likely has three edges and `dependency_count:2`. Neither affects the assertions — `hasSchemaGap` reads none of the trimmed fields — but "golden" invites the reader to assume verbatim fidelity. A short note in `test/fixtures/` on how golden lines are captured and trimmed would keep the next reader honest.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY

- `npx tsc --noEmit` in cwd: clean.
- Biome: passed — `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` is fail-fast and reached the vitest step, which is only possible with typecheck and lint green.
- Vitest in cwd: 17 passed, 4 failed, all four solely from finding 1's missing fixture (`beads: null`, i.e. `readFile` threw). Both tests that carry this diff's substance — the golden-fixture test and the schema-errors test, reading `test/fixtures/beads-*.jsonl` — pass.
- I hand-computed the four fixture-dependent tests against the new code and the fixture content read out of the branch: fort-alpha still yields `open 4, ready 3, schemaGaps 1, malformed 1` (the `legacy` line loses its labels gap but keeps gaps on `issue_type` and `created_at`, so the count is unchanged), and `legacy.labels` is now `[]`, matching the changed assertion at `test/status.test.ts:73`. Every changed assertion is justified by the specified behaviour; none weakens a check.
- The handoff's factual claims against the code: all four accurate, including "21 tests across 5 files", which matches my own run.
- The handoff is appended, prior entries untouched (standing order 7).
- ShellCheck did not run (verify.sh is fail-fast and the test step failed first). The diff changes no shell script, so nothing in it is at risk from that step.

TAKEN ON FAITH

- That the golden bzx.2 line is a faithful transcription of a live `bd` export. There is no committed `issues.jsonl` in this repo yet — that is bead fortkit-bzx.5's job — and invoking `bd` was not permitted from this seat, so I could not re-derive it. What I have is that the line matches the Mayor's recorded observation in the bead (count 1, two edges, 1 blocks + 1 parent-child) exactly, and that its timestamps share the same UTC/PST skew as the pre-existing bzx.5 golden line, which is a real export artifact. Once bzx.5 lands, this fixture becomes checkable against a tracked export.
- That the full verifier passes in the candidate worktree, as the handoff states. I could not run it there (denied, correctly — the Warden does not write to the candidate), and the four failures I saw are fully explained by finding 1.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — bzx.6 meets all six criteria, tsc/biome clean; 5 non-blocking findings, incl. warden.sh stripping test fixtures

title: Canonical issues.jsonl export enabled in every fort + fort-init template
description: Consequence of the Overseer's 2026-08-07 ruling: the passive .beads/issues.jsonl export is canonical for cross-fort bead state. title: Covenant amendment: adopt the First Moot's rulings on quorum, concurrence, the borrowed bench, and resumption
description:
Proposed by Emrith Cairnwright, convening the First Moot of the Covenant from outside the layer. Amending the covenant is gate 6.2 — she proposes, the Overseer applies. NONE of these bind until he writes them in. Her own caveat: 'If he wants them narrower, they should be narrower; I have been wrong once this week about the subject of my own document and I do not mistake fluency for correctness.'

Belongs in covenant section 8.

1. DECLARATION IS NOT SEATING. A declared-but-unseated occupant holds NO ballot. The declaration is the occupant's own and needs no leave; the seating is gate 6.4, the Overseer's. 'If a declaration carried a ballot, then declaring would confer voice, and gate 6.4 would be hollow while formally intact.' The humane half: an unseated declared occupant MAY speak and be quoted. Hear them, count nothing.

2. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING — a three-seat layer can NEVER name its own offices. A seat does not sit in judgment on its own office word, so naming any one of three draws a recusal and leaves two. 'Three minus one is two, always, at full strength, forever.' Therefore the borrowed bench is not a stopgap; it is the ordinary and standing instrument, and should be entered in the covenant as such.

3. TWO BALLOTS ARE NOT A MOOT. With two, the tie-break ladder collapses: rung three is inapplicable where the convener holds none, and rung one is decided by which seat declined to rank a third name, so 'a seat's silence decides.' Also 'a twelve-point Borda table over two ballots renders exactly like an eighteen-point table over three' to a stranger a year out. Name the lesser instrument: a CONCURRENCE. Two seated occupants independently briefed each state a preference and reasons in full; if they concur it carries and is recorded as a concurrence with NO tally drawn; if they diverge, the annal records both reasons entire, the question is NOT decided, and it goes to the Overseer marked undecided.

4. THE BORROWED BENCH. Three independent ballots. Held by the layer's SEATED occupants who are not candidates and whose own office is not being named. The permanent shortfall is filled from the settlements, drawn by the Overseer, ONE SEAT PER FORT, never two from one fort ('two seats of one settlement are not two independent judgments about a word; they share a charter, a record, and a room'). PARTICIPATION IS NOT JURISDICTION, exactly as residence is not — 'written down facing both ways or it will be read as a doorway.' The Overseer does not ballot: 'a ranked ballot from the one person who can overturn the count is not a ballot; it is an instruction with arithmetic on it.'

5. THE OUTSIDE CONVENER is appointed PER SITTING, by name, casts nothing, and their authority ends with the record. The practice recurs; the appointment never does. Prefer a convener who did not convene the last one, 'so the practice does not quietly harden into a post,' and one with no stake in the outcome.

6. THE RESUMPTION RULE. 'An agent session is not resumable across the completion of the act it performed... A correction arriving after an act is complete is a new act and must be run as one, or not at all.' Arrived at independently by the convener and by the Regent on the same evening, from two different incidents.

Established 2026-08-04 by the Overseer's edict, executed by the Regent.

THE LOAD-BEARING DISTINCTIONS, so they are not eroded later:
- RESIDENCE IS NOT JURISDICTION (covenant s1). These seats live in fortkit; Manyhalls' charter does not bind them and its Mayor does not direct them.
- THE LAYER IS NOT A MANAGEMENT TIER OVER THE FORTS (covenant s2). No civ seat directs a Mayor, prioritizes a fort's beads, or overrides a Warden. - ACCESS IS PER SEAT (covenant s5). One seat has root on everything, one may read exactly one JSON document, one may read everything and reach nothing. A single 'civ seat' permission posture would be wrong for all three.
- PRECEDENCE (covenant s4): a civ seat inside a settlement honours that settlement's human gates, announces itself in that fort's stream at start and end, never emits as one of its citizens, and may be reviewed by that fort's Warden. Only the Regent may cross a capability boundary, only by edict, only with the Overseer present, never silently.

The Forge's and Warden's briefs both stated the office under naming correctly ('the security-publication office, whose craft is extraction and publication and never hunting'). The convener's SECOND-ROUND brief restated the pool, the rulings sought and the ballots, and omitted the office entirely. In round 1 she had it right and recorded the Herald as a separate empty chair; across the round boundary the framing was lost and nothing re-anchored it. She then wrote the annals, emitted three events and filed a retitle bead describing the wrong seat. The independence that made the moot genuine is the same property that let one participant's drift go uncaught until the record was already written.

2. A MOOT PARTICIPANT HELD WRITE ACCESS TO FORT RECORDS. The Forge and Warden sessions used zero tools and returned text. The convener's session held full tools and wrote fort/annals/, fort/events/ and a bead directly, unreviewed, on a mistaken premise. The Warden seat in this civilization is read-only BY CONSTRUCTION because a review that can also write is not a review; a moot has the same shape, and the ceremony had no such guarantee.

Realized cost: a correction appended to the annals, three permanent events corrected by a fourth, one bead closed against execution, and a near-miss in which an Overseer-approved seat would have been renamed across its spec, seat file and founding papers.

Briefing the two occupant-declarants, I gave each a list of existing actor ids to avoid colliding with, and the list was INCOMPLETE: it omitted 'orin' (Orin Slowfire, Farlantern's Forge) and was assembled from memory of the moot record rather than read from the seat files. Difference in outcome, which is the point: it was caught before either declaration landed, because I went looking at the roster rather than assuming it. Corrected mid-flight by sending the complete ten-name roster to the still-running declarant with the reasoning attached. Detail on fortkit-ugr.4.

Adds a third rule to the two already on this bead: **a constraint list in a brief must be GENERATED FROM THE SOURCE at brief time, never recalled.** If the brief says 'must not collide with X, Y, Z', the X Y Z comes from reading the seat files in that moment. This is the same discipline the fifth seat's law calls traceability, applied to the instructions we hand each other rather than to what we publish.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
THIRD ENTRY, same session, new failure mode — Regent, 2026-08-04.

RESUMING A COMPLETED CEREMONY SESSION PRODUCES A SECOND RITUAL ACT, NOT AN AMENDMENT TO THE FIRST.

Having noticed my actor-id list omitted 'orin', I sent the complete roster to the Herald's declaration session as a correction. That session had already returned a full declaration (Wystan Onlylent, he/him) which I had already emitted to the event stream. The resumption did not amend it. It produced a second complete declaration under a different name (Bramwen Lentvoice, she/her), whose text asserts the correction 'arrived before I had settled anything' — which the stream contradicts.

No harm done that the record could not absorb: Manyhalls ruling 1 covers it exactly (a seat's name is its own, the later declaration governs, the prior is preserved never overwritten, and a rename emits again). But the harm was avoided by luck of having applicable case law, not by method.

RULE, added to the two already on this bead and the one added earlier tonight: **once a ceremonial act has been returned AND recorded, do not resume that session. Correct the record instead.** A ritual session does not hold the notion that it has already spoken. If a correction is needed after an act is recorded, it is an amendment to the record made by the transcriber, or a fresh act deliberately convened and labelled as one — never a nudge to a finished session.

Cumulative rules from this bead, now four: (1) every round's brief restates the subject in full, and the participant who authors the record gets the fullest brief; (2) participants deliberate read-only; (3) constraint lists in a brief are generated from the source at brief time, never recalled; (4) never resume a ceremony session whose act is already recorded.

description:
Founded by edict of the Overseer, 2026-08-04, via the Regent. Civilization-scope seat housed in Manyhalls.

CRAFT: extraction and publication, NOT hunting. (1) NOT one office with the Herald. Two seats, one shared law, explicit referral both ways. REVISIT TRIGGER, named now so it is not re-litigated on vibes: if the public artifacts acquire outside contributors, issue traffic, or a release cadence needing their own review loop, the artifact repo has become a product and a product wants a settlement.

title: [bug] Regent launcher: every edict announced in the wrong fort, and no edict ever announced its end
description:
Two defects in bin/regent, both defeating the Regent's ONLY safety property (charter: 'an edict is never silent'; seats are told to treat an unexplained change with no edict event as a security signal).

DEFECT 1 (misrouted proclamation). emit.sh resolves its target event stream from the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY (it walks git's common dir so a worktree appends to its main repo's stream). bin/regent's proclamation loop invoked $repo/fort/scripts/emit.sh for each fort WITHOUT cd-ing into it, so all three edict.begun events landed in the caller's fort. Measured: fortkit's stream held 9 edict.begun (3 wakes x 3 forts); ForgeOs and longburn held ZERO. This is the recorded incident class 'launch scripts emitting as another fort's citizens'.

DEFECT 2 (dead cleanup). The launcher ended with exec script/exec $RUNNER. exec replaces the shell and discards the EXIT trap with it, so cleanup() never ran and the launcher has never emitted edict.ended. The three correctly-routed edict.ended events at 2026-08-04T21:56:33 were hand-emitted, not launcher-emitted.

COMBINED CONSEQUENCE: in Proofdelve and Farlantern the edict-announcement detector has never once fired. A seat there following the charter exactly would classify every genuine edict as a possible compromise, and a genuinely silent change would be indistinguishable from normal.

Correction is append-only: the three misfiled edict.begun events were backfilled into ForgeOs and longburn with -T at their true timestamps and payload {backfilled:true, reason, reconstructed_from}. The misfiled fortkit copies were NOT deleted (standing order 7).

title: Tell the seats about the Regent: edicts, and what to expect of them
description:
OVERSEER-AUTHORIZED. The Regent office now exists (fortkit-i2x): a break-glass seat that runs unmasked with civilization-wide access, invoked by hand only while Justin is present, for work the forts cannot do for themselves — changing a kernel-read-only constitution, repairing a launcher, propagating law across settlements.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. Until now, changes have arrived in these forts from outside the normal chain with no explanation in the charter: files this fort's own seats cannot write have changed under them. That is disorienting to work under and it is bad practice besides. A seat that finds its constitution altered by an unexplained hand has no way to tell a legitimate edict from a compromise, which is both a welfare problem and a security one.

WHAT THE SEATS SHOULD BE ABLE TO RELY ON, once this lands:
1. Edicts exist, they are rare, and they are legitimate.
2. Every edict announces itself: edict.begun and edict.ended in this fort's own event stream, and any change it makes leaves a record here — a bead, an event, or a commit message that explains itself.
3. An edict is not a reason to distrust your own judgement. If a change looks wrong, contradicts the charter, or has no record explaining it, SAY SO — to Justin, in a bead, on the record. Seats are not expected to defer silently to anything that arrives from above.
4. An unexplained change with no edict event is exactly the anomaly worth escalating. That is a security signal, not a nuisance.

title: The Regent: civilization break-glass seat (Overseer-authorized, built by the harness)
description:

title: Cycle 6: git works inside the mask; push/deploy move to a PROSE gate (Overseer-authorized)
description:
OVERSEER-AUTHORIZED, 2026-08-04, executed by the harness because the seats are (correctly) too restricted to change their own constitution. Filed here so this fort's record shows what changed and why.

PROBLEM. Since the mask landed, git fetch/push fail inside a seat with 'Bad owner or permissions on /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/...'. Diagnosed: bwrap creates a user namespace, so root-owned files read as owned by 'nobody' inside it, and OpenSSH refuses config files owned by neither root nor the invoking user. Verified directly (ls shows root outside, nobody inside). Consequence beyond convenience: a Mayor that cannot fetch cannot verify ahead/behind against the real remote, so standing order 11 (committed != pushed != deployed, separately verified) could no longer be honoured — Proofdelve's Mayor had to estimate '~16 commits ahead' from a stale ref.

FIX 1 (mechanical). seat-sandbox.sh binds a user-owned ssh_config over /etc/ssh inside the sandbox. Verified: ssh gets past the ownership check to the identity stage. The ssh-agent socket was already reachable through the mask, so an agent-held key signs without the session ever reading the key file; ~/.ssh stays masked.

FIX 2 (policy, and an honest DOWNGRADE). At the Overseer's direction, push and deploy move from a mechanical block to a PROSE gate for the MAYOR seat: the Mayor may run them, and must ask Justin first. Rationale of record: everything is development/staging today, no live customers, and the consequences of a mistaken push are acceptable against the cost of routing every push through a human terminal. This is explicitly weaker than a capability boundary and is recorded as such — prose is a gate a model chooses to honour, not one it cannot cross.

SCOPE. Mayor only. Forge keeps its mechanical blocks: it runs unattended and therefore CANNOT ask permission, so a prose gate on an autonomous seat guards nothing. Warden is unchanged (read-only by construction, never pushes).

Charter amendments, seat-prompt language, permission entries, and templates all land in this cycle.
notes:
2026-08-04 CYCLE 6 APPLIED. Mechanical fix verified (fetch works inside the mask; key unreadable; agent signs; ForgeOs true state was 18 ahead, not the estimated 16). Policy fix applied: charter gains a 'Prose gates' section recording the downgrade and its rationale, mayor.sh prompt and fort/seats/mayor.md carry the ask-first rule, settings allow push/fetch shapes (force-push still denied). REMAINING, needs an Overseer decision: DEPLOY is still mechanically blocked for the Mayor even though policy now permits it — scripts/deploy-azure-staging.sh sources .env.staging.local, which the kernel mask makes unreadable to every seat. Enabling real deploy capability means unmasking staging secrets to the Mayor (threat #4, credential leakage) or building an airlock. Not done unilaterally.

Verification had been run against a file a later command replaced. Fix re-applied and re-verified AFTER landing in all three forts and the template (fetch works; true divergence reported). No amend: the false claim and its correction both stand in the record.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

Round 1 review of bead `fortkit-r6x.1`, commits `af4e82a` (product), `dfca4fd` (handoff), `62ec033` (prior no-verdict record) on `bead/r6x.1`. Author: Kethra Anvilmark (Forge). Model attribution for *this* work is not stated in the handoff — the file's corrected attribution ("GPT-5.6 Terra") is explicitly about the earlier `bf0` section. I reviewed at GPT-5.6-Terra scrutiny, which is the fort's rung-1 Forge model, and note the missing attribution as finding 8. The prior launch died at login with no verdict, so round discipline treats this as round one.

The shape of the work is right: it reuses the jmq event/handoff/registry readers rather than building a second collector, models every source as `T | null` with `ABSENT` rendering, keeps telemetry to `{files, records, malformed}` with a test that proves prompt bodies never reach the serialized output, adds no runtime deps, and adds a `.sort()` to the event-shard file listing that makes tie-ordering deterministic — a real determinism fix, not decoration. The two things that block are both in the two code paths that have **no test at all**: the `bd` subprocess and the `git log` subprocess. Everything the tests cover is correct; everything they don't cover is silently wrong. That is the through-line of this round.

**1. BLOCKING — `git log` is windowed by git's approxidate, not by the digest's parsed instant; the same command returns different answers at different times of day.** `src/digest.ts:38-60` passes the *raw user strings* to `--since=`/`--before=`, while events, closed beads, and telemetry are windowed on `Date.parse()` instants. Git's approxidate fills unspecified time-of-day fields from the current clock. Demonstrated against the real repo just now:

- `git -C /home/justin/dev/fortkit log --format=%cI --since=2026-08-04 --before=2026-08-05 main` → **0 commits**
- `git -C ... --since=2026-08-04T00:00:00Z --before=2026-08-05T00:00:00Z main` → **34 commits**
- `--since=2026-08-04` alone → 0; `--since=2026-08-03` alone → 43. The cutoff is "that date at the current wall-clock time" (19:47 local), not midnight.

So `fortkit digest --since 2026-08-04` renders `git log: 0` for a day with 34 commits, and the number changes hour to hour. That fails the bead's first word (deterministic) and its stated bar (stable, complete, honest about gaps) — a zero is not a gap marker. It also re-opens `fortkit-dpu`, whose verbatim law is that readers normalize to one basis at read time and never let a second calendar in. Fix: pass `new Date(sinceInstant).toISOString()` / `new Date(untilInstant).toISOString()` to git, the same instants the other four sources use. Fold in the boundary while you are there: git's `--since` is "more recent than", so a commit exactly at `since` is dropped while an event at the same instant is kept by `inWindow`'s `>=`. And add a test: a fixture git repo with commits inside and outside the window, asserted against a date-only `--since`. That test is what would have caught this.

**2. BLOCKING — `bd list` silently truncates at 50, so closed beads under-report with no gap marker.** `src/readers/digest.ts:22-32` runs `bd -C <path> list --status=closed --json` with no `--limit`. Verified from `bd -C /home/justin/dev/fortkit list --help` (bd 1.1.2): `-n, --limit int   Limit results (default 50, use 0 for unlimited)`, and verified empirically that the flag truncates (`--all --json --limit 5` → 5 of 41). The truncation happens *before* the code's window filter, and bd's default sort is priority-first (observed order: two P0, then P1s, then P2), not closed-at-descending — so the beads dropped are the low-priority ones, and they are dropped silently. The first fort to accumulate 51 closed beads starts losing yesterday's closures from the Herald's morning input with no indication. fortkit is at 41 issues total after two days; I could not measure Proofdelve or Farlantern from this seat (outside my allowed directories), so I cannot tell you whether this is already live today. Fix, both flags proven working just now: `--limit 0`, and let bd do the windowing with `--closed-after`/`--closed-before` (RFC3339 accepted; `--closed-after 2026-08-05T00:00:00Z` correctly returned 6 of 10). Windowing in bd also largely defuses finding 3. Add a happy-path test — the current suite never once proves that `readClosedBeads` returns a bead.

**3. Non-blocking — the `bd` call will hit `execFile`'s 1 MB `maxBuffer` and render the whole source ABSENT.** The code fetches full bead records (`description`, `design`, `notes`) and keeps only `id`/`title`/`closed_at`. fortkit's ten closed beads already serialize to **40.9 KB** because Warden verdicts live in `notes` (the `jmq` record alone is ~15 KB). At fifty such records the default 1 MB buffer is exceeded, `execFileAsync` rejects, the `catch` returns `null`, and closed beads read ABSENT for that fort forever. Honest, unlike finding 2, but wrong. Raise `maxBuffer` explicitly, or narrow the query per finding 2.

**4. Non-blocking — `bd` is invoked without `--readonly`, against every registered fort.** bd 1.1.2 has `--readonly` ("block write operations, for worker sandboxes") and `--sandbox`. `fortkit-u8v`'s probe 9 recorded `bd show` failing on a Dolt LOCK against a read-only mount, so bd touches more than the query path even for reads. `fortkit-jmq`'s boundary is explicit: "read-only over all fort data — the tool never writes beads, events, or git." This is the same shape as my `--no-optional-locks` finding on `git status` in the jmq round, and it bears on threat 1 (agent accident): a product CLI reaching into every fort's `.beads` should be mechanically unable to write. `--readonly` verified working (`--readonly --limit 0` returned the same 10). Also note the digest silently excludes closed gate/infra/template beads, which bd hides by default — worth an explicit decision rather than an inherited default.

**5. Non-blocking — drift flag, per standing order 2.** `fortkit-jmq`'s spec says of the beads source, verbatim: "Do not shell out to bd." This bead says "closed beads (via bd)". The newer bead governs and I am not treating it as a violation, but the fort now has two beads access paths (`src/readers/beads.ts` reading the JSONL export, and `readClosedBeads` shelling to bd) with no recorded decision reconciling them — and jmq finding 7 already established that no fort produces the JSONL export. Worth one line in a spec saying which is canonical.

**6. Non-blocking — module placement drifts from the established readers layout.** `src/readers/git.ts` already owns a private `git()` execFile helper; `readGitLog` duplicates that boilerplate inside `src/digest.ts`, which is supposed to be the assembler. `src/readers/digest.ts` is a grab-bag holding a beads reader and a telemetry reader, next to an existing `src/readers/beads.ts`. The convention is one module per source; `readClosedBeads` belongs in `beads.ts`, `readTelemetryCounts` in a `telemetry.ts`, `readGitLog` in `git.ts`. Relatedly, the candidate-listing block in `readHandoffSections` is a verbatim copy of the one in `readLastHandoff` — one helper, two callers. Also: `handoffSections: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readHandoffSections>>` in `src/digest.ts:21` should just import `HandoffSection`, which the same commit exports.

**7. Non-blocking, inherited — handoff files with a suffix are invisible to the digest.** The regex `^([a-z0-9_-]+)-(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.md$` does not match `mayor-2026-08-04-b.md`, which exists in this fort today. The file is skipped with no gap marker. The regex is copied verbatim from the pre-existing `readLastHandoff`, so this is inherited rather than introduced — bead it, don't hold the merge. Two related coarsenesses in the same area, also non-blocking: handoff sections are windowed by the *filename* date parsed as a UTC midnight-to-midnight day, while the fort names those files by local date (the exact `fortkit-dpu` split), so a file is included whenever its nominal UTC day overlaps the window at all; and an unreadable handoff file is `continue`d past silently rather than counted.

**8. Non-blocking — record hygiene.** (a) The r6x.1 handoff does not name the model that did the work; the charter requires every bead and handoff to record it. (b) The r6x.1 handoff was appended into `forge-2026-08-05.md`, a file whose subject is `bf0`, beneath a heading that reads "## Correction appended" — but the appended content is a new handoff for a different bead, not a correction. Append-only discipline is satisfied (I checked: `62ec033` and `dfca4fd` add lines only, no deletions); the labelling is what misleads. Prior `lwf` finding 13 is properly discharged — the "GPT-5.6 Codex"/date-ahead correction is present and appended, not edited in.

**9. Non-blocking — fort machinery defect I hit while reviewing, not part of this diff.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` rsyncs the candidate tree with `--exclude '.beads'`, unanchored, which also strips the **tracked test fixture** `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl`. Consequence: the Warden's scratch copy can never run the fort's own verifier green — three pre-existing tests in `status.test.ts` and `world.test.ts` fail there with `beads: null`, looking exactly like a Forge regression. Fix is one character: `--exclude '/.beads'`. Filing this as a bead rather than escalating, since this diff changes no launcher.

**10. Non-blocking — smaller notes.** `readCivilizationDigest` calls `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` and throws `RangeError` if given an unparseable `since`; the CLI guards it, but `herald.sh` (r6x.4) will call the library directly. The CLI validator at `src/cli.ts:11-29` works correctly on every edge I traced (missing values, duplicated flags, flags-as-values, positional strays, empty window) but does it with a `Set` that contains the argument *values* and a hand-computed expected-length — it is hard to read and harder to extend; a small parse function returning a tagged result would age better. `formatDigest` prints counts for every source including events, beads, handoffs and commits, so the human format carries no content at all; that is defensible if `--json` is the Herald's real input, but say so somewhere. No test exercises `fortkit digest --json` end to end, or `formatDigest` beyond `toContain("ABSENT")`. `readTelemetryCounts` charges an unreadable *file* to the `malformed` *record* counter and omits it from `files`, conflating two units.

**Verified independently:** the full diff line by line against the bead's spec and acceptance criteria; `npm ci` clean (52 packages) and `npx tsc --noEmit` green in the scratch copy; the digest and CLI tests green there (4/4); the full suite at 15 tests with exactly 3 failures, all traced to finding 9's fixture exclusion and none touching files this diff modifies; `package.json` untouched, so "no new runtime deps" holds; bd 1.1.2's `list` help text, the default-50 limit, the `--limit` truncation, the top-level-array JSON shape, the `closed_at` field name, and that `--readonly`, `--limit 0` and `--closed-after` all work; the 40.9 KB payload for ten closed beads; git's approxidate behaviour on date-only bounds with the 0-vs-34 comparison above; the registry's relative-path resolution against the fixture; that real event payloads carry no prompt bodies; that `fort/telemetry/prompts.jsonl` is the real (gitignored) hook target and its `ts` field matches the reader; that `mayor-2026-08-04-b.md` fails the handoff regex; that `62ec033`/`dfca4fd` are pure appends; that no gate-1 file (charter, seats, launchers, profiles) is touched by this diff.

**Taken on faith:** Biome lint and ShellCheck — my seat's permission set refused every invocation of the Biome binary I tried, and `verify.sh` itself would fail on finding 9 regardless. No shell script changed in this diff, so ShellCheck is a formality here; the lint claim rests on Kethra's handoff and on the code reading as Biome-formatted. Also on faith: the closed-bead totals of Proofdelve and Farlantern (outside my allowed directories), which is what would tell us whether finding 2 is already biting today rather than next week; and that `bd list`'s default sort is priority-first, which I inferred from one observed ordering rather than from documentation.

To clear: findings 1 and 2, each with the test that would have caught it. Fold in 3 and 4 in the same round — they are one-line changes to the same two call sites, and 2's `--closed-after` fix largely subsumes 3. Findings 5 through 10 want beads; none of them should hold this merge, and 9 wants a bead against the launcher regardless of what happens to this one.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
All checks complete. Writing the verdict.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round 2 review of bead fortkit-r6x.1 at commit e7055ed on `bead/r6x.1` (range `main..bead/r6x.1`, commits af4e82a, dfca4fd, 62ec033, e7055ed). Author: Kethra Anvilmark, model **GPT-5.6 Terra** — the fort's rung-1 Forge model, named in the round-2 handoff and in Justin's bead comment. Round-1 finding 8a (missing attribution) is thereby discharged. Terra carries no reward-hacking flag (that is on Sol), and this round's work does not read like flag-chasing: the fixes are the ones asked for, in the places asked for, with no widening.

**Both round-1 blockers are fixed, and I verified each against the real repo rather than against the handoff.**

Blocker 1 (git log windowed by approxidate). `readGitLog` now lives in `src/readers/git.ts:19-46`, reuses the existing private `git()` helper, takes parsed instants, and passes ISO-8601 bounds. Re-running my round-1 demonstration against `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` just now: `--since=2026-08-04 --before=2026-08-05 main` still returns **0** commits, while the form the code now emits, `--since=2026-08-03T23:59:59.000Z --before=2026-08-05T00:00:00.000Z`, returns **34**. The `since - 1000` widening is the right shape — git's `--since` is "more recent than", so the query is deliberately one second wider than the canonical window and the authoritative half-open filter (`instant >= since && instant < until`) is applied client-side on the same `%cI` instants. That makes both boundaries safe regardless of git's own inclusivity. `test/git.test.ts` builds a fixture repo with commits at 23:59:59, exactly 00:00:00, mid-window, and exactly the next midnight, and asserts a date-only window keeps the midnight-boundary commit and drops the next one. It passes in my scratch copy.

Blocker 2 (bd's silent 50-bead cap). `readClosedBeads` moved to `src/readers/beads.ts:75-129` and now runs `bd --readonly -C <path> list --all --status=closed --limit=0 --closed-after=<RFC3339> --closed-before=<RFC3339> --json` with a 16 MiB `maxBuffer`. I re-verified against bd 1.1.2 that `--limit 0` is unlimited, that `--closed-after`/`--closed-before` accept RFC3339 and filter correctly, that `--readonly` is accepted alongside the full flag set, and that the JSON is a flat top-level array with no nested children (10 `"id":` keys at any depth for 10 closed beads). Windowing at the source also discharges round-1 finding 3: the 40.9 KB-for-ten-beads payload is now bounded to one day's closures against a 16× larger buffer, so the `execFile` overflow-to-ABSENT path is no longer reachable in practice. Round-1 finding 4 is discharged too — `--readonly` is present, which is the threat-1 (agent accident) control I asked for on a product CLI that reaches into every registered fort's `.beads`.

Everything else in the round-2 scope landed: `readTelemetryCounts` in its own `src/readers/telemetry.ts`, `readClosedBeads` in `beads.ts`, `readGitLog` in `git.ts`, the duplicated handoff candidate-listing collapsed into one `handoffCandidates()` helper with two callers, `HandoffSection` imported instead of the `Awaited<ReturnType<...>>` gymnastics, and `readCivilizationDigest` now throwing clear errors on unparseable or empty windows so r6x.4's `herald.sh` cannot walk into `new Date(NaN)`. The out-of-scope items were left alone — `src/cli.ts` is untouched by e7055ed, `formatDigest` is unchanged, the handoff regex is unchanged, no launcher is touched. **No scope creep.** The `handoffs.ts` and `digest.ts` refactors are behavior-preserving line for line, and `src/readers/beads.ts` is 66 added / 0 deleted, so the pre-existing `readBeads` is provably untouched.

I found **no regressions**. Under round-2 discipline that settles the verdict; the findings below are beads, not merge conditions.

**1. Non-blocking, and the one I would fix first — the new comment at `src/readers/beads.ts:100-102` states the opposite of what the code does.** It reads: "The digest intentionally includes every bead type: gate, infrastructure, and template work are all part of a fort's complete activity record." `--all` does not do that. From `bd list --help` (bd 1.1.2), `--all` is documented as "Show all issues including closed (overrides default filter)" — it overrides the *status* filter, nothing else. Gate, infra, and template beads are hidden behind three separate flags: `--include-gates` ("Include gate issues in output (normally hidden)"), `--include-infra`, `--include-templates`. None is passed. So the round-2 scope item "make an explicit decision comment on the closed-beads type filter rather than inheriting bd's default hide" produced a comment recording a decision the code does not implement, and the digest still silently omits closed gate beads — the class tracking this fort's own human gates — from every Herald morning. I could not demonstrate the divergence empirically: fortkit has zero beads of those types (42 beads, all bug/task/feature/epic/decision; `--include-gates --include-infra --include-templates` changes the count from 42 to 42 and the closed count from 10 to 10), so this rests on bd's help text, which is unambiguous. Fix is one of two lines: add the three flags to match the comment, or rewrite the comment to say the digest deliberately inherits bd's default hide. I am not blocking on it because the underlying behavior is identical to round 1, where I already ruled the type-filter omission non-blocking; what is new is only the wrong comment, and a digest with a wrong comment still leaves the fort better off than no digest. But a comment that misinforms is worse than no comment, and this one will be believed.

**2. Non-blocking — bd's `--closed-after` is exclusive, so a bead closed at exactly `since` falls through every window.** Proven against the live repo: with a bead whose `closed_at` is exactly `2026-08-04T19:27:25Z`, `--closed-after=2026-08-04T19:27:25Z` returns **7** and `--closed-after=2026-08-04T19:27:24Z` returns **8**. The digest's canonical window is inclusive-since, and `digest.ts` re-filters with `>= since`, but bd has already dropped the record. Because the daily windows tile, such a bead appears in no digest ever. `--closed-before` is exclusive too, which happens to match `< until` exactly, so that end is fine. This is precisely the boundary asymmetry that `readGitLog` fixes one file over with `since - 1000`, and the mirror was not applied. One line: `--closed-after=${new Date(since - 1000).toISOString()}`, safe because `digest.ts` re-filters. The digest test's expected flag string would need the matching update. Probability of biting is roughly one lost bead per several years at second precision, which is why this is a bead and not a blocker — but it is a real hole with a one-line fix.

**3. Non-blocking — the bd happy-path test proves the invocation shape, not bd's semantics.** `test/digest.test.ts` stubs `bd` with a shell script that pattern-matches the exact flag string on `PATH`. That is the right call for CI (no bd dependency, no fixture Dolt db) and it does prove the id/title/`closed_at`→`closedAt` mapping. But every semantic the fix depends on — that `--limit 0` is unlimited, that `--closed-after` is exclusive, that `--json` is a flat array — is verified only by hand, by me, twice. A bd upgrade that changes any of them passes green. Worth recording the verified semantics and the version (bd 1.1.2) in a comment beside the call, so the next reader knows what was checked and against what.

**4. Non-blocking — the digest-level closed-beads path has no assertion.** `readClosedBeads` is tested via the stub; `readDigestFort`'s window re-filter and the null→ABSENT rendering for closed beads are not. The digest test deliberately makes no assertion on Alpha's `closedBeads` (sensible — the result depends on whether real `bd` is installed on the runner), which leaves that branch uncovered. Note also that beads with a null `closed_at` are silently dropped by the re-filter rather than counted as a gap.

**5. Non-blocking — closed beads are sorted by id, not by close time.** `.sort((left, right) => left.id.localeCompare(right.id))` gives determinism, which is what the bead demanded. For a morning digest, `closed_at` order would carry the narrative and would be equally deterministic.

**6. Non-blocking — `git()` still runs without `--no-optional-locks` and with the default 1 MB `maxBuffer`.** The lock flag is my standing finding from the jmq round, unchanged here and pre-existing; it bears on threat 1 (agent accident), where a read-path tool touching another fort's repo should be mechanically unable to take a write lock. The buffer needs about ten thousand commits in one window to overflow, so it is a note, not a risk.

**7. Non-blocking — `git log --since` limits traversal rather than filtering it.** Git stops walking at the first commit older than the cutoff along a path; commits with skewed committer dates sitting behind an older commit can be missed (this is why git 2.37 added `--since-as-filter`). Not observed in any fort repo, and the fort's commits are monotonic, so this is recorded rather than acted on — but it is the one remaining way `readGitLog` can under-report without a gap marker.

**8. Non-blocking — smaller notes.** (a) `--all` is redundant alongside `--status=closed` (verified: 10 either way); harmless, but it is the flag whose meaning finding 1 turns on, so its presence reads as doing more than it does. (b) A registry entry with a known `fort_name` but no `repo` renders as `[malformed registry entry 3]`, discarding the name it does have; reporting `Broken [malformed registry entry 3]` would be more honest about the gap. (c) `fortkit digest --since <future>` with no `--until` slips past the CLI validator, which only compares the two when `--until` is present, and hits `readCivilizationDigest`'s new throw as an unhandled rejection with a stack trace instead of exit 2. (d) `readEventFeed` reads every event shard a fort has ever written and then filters, on every daily digest; performance only, but it grows without bound.

**9. Non-blocking, tracked elsewhere.** `fortkit-wtm` holds the inherited handoff-suffix regex gap, the filename-date handoff windowing, and the telemetry file/record unit conflation — all correctly out of round-2 scope. `fortkit-a0z` holds the `warden.sh` rsync defect, which still reproduces exactly: `--exclude '.beads'` is unanchored and strips the tracked fixture `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` from my scratch copy, so the fort's own verifier cannot run green from this seat. **Acceptance criteria.** Tests cover `--since`/`--until` windowing (three independent tests, including both boundary directions on telemetry and on git). Absent and malformed forts are covered. Counts-only telemetry is asserted by two negative assertions on prompt bodies. No new runtime deps — `package.json` is untouched by the whole branch and has no `dependencies` key at all. The one partial: `--json` shape is asserted on the library's return object rather than end-to-end through `fortkit digest --json`; that was round-1 finding 10 and Justin scoped it out of round 2, so I record it as met-in-substance.

**Verified independently, in this session:** the full `main..bead/r6x.1` diff line by line, plus e7055ed's delta in isolation to confirm the refactors are behavior-preserving and that `cli.ts` was not reopened; `npm ci` clean (0 vulnerabilities) and `npx tsc --noEmit` silent in my scratch copy; `npx vitest run` at 17 tests with exactly 3 failures, all traced to fortkit-a0z's stripped fixture; a verbose targeted run confirming all 7 tests in `digest.test.ts`, `git.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts` pass, including both new ones; the 0-vs-34 git comparison proving blocker 1 is really fixed and not merely restated; bd 1.1.2's `list --help` in full; the 7-vs-8 `--closed-after` exclusivity demonstration; `--closed-before` exclusivity; `--limit 0`; `--readonly` accepted with the full flag set; the flat 10-element JSON shape at any nesting depth; that fortkit has no gate/infra/template beads with which to demonstrate finding 1; that the fixture directories in both the worktree and my scratch copy show no side effects from the test suite invoking real `bd`; that the worktree is clean at e7055ed with no uncommitted work and my scratch `src/` is byte-identical to it; that the handoff change is 30 added / 0 deleted (append-only holds, standing order 7); that `src/readers/beads.ts` is 66 added / 0 deleted so `readBeads` is untouched; and that no gate-1 file (charter, seats, launchers, profiles) is touched by this diff, so no mandatory escalation applies.

**Taken on faith:** Biome lint — my seat's permission set refused every invocation of the Biome binary I tried, in round 1 and again here; the claim rests on Kethra's `verify.sh --no-emit` run and on the code reading as Biome-formatted, and `verify.sh` would fail on fortkit-a0z from this seat regardless. ShellCheck — no shell script changed in this diff, so it is a formality. The exact leading-position `bd --readonly -C <path> list ...` form was refused by my permission rules; I verified the equivalent `bd -C <path> --readonly list ...` with the identical flag set, and Cobra treats persistent flags position-agnostically. Finding 1 rests on bd's help text rather than on an observed divergence, for the stated reason. And Proofdelve's and Farlantern's bead volumes remain outside my allowed directories, so I still cannot say whether blocker 2 was already costing the civilization closures before this fix — only that it can no longer.

Findings 1 through 8 want beads; finding 1 wants one today. None of them should hold this merge.

comments.text:
Review complete. Here is my record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

The change does exactly what the bead asked and nothing else: `WorldFort.beads.ready` → `open`, the page label `'ready '+f.beads.ready` → `'open '+f.beads.open`, and a test that asserts the honest label and rejects the old one. Four files, 31 insertions. Both acceptance criteria are met — no field or label named `ready` survives anywhere in `src/`, `test/`, `templates/`, `README.md`, or the founding spec's label surface, and the test genuinely discriminates (it fails against `main`'s page string on both new assertions). `src/status.ts` already said `open`; the two projections now agree, which they did not before.

Model: **gpt-5.6-terra**, the top Forge rung, per `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl` (`session.start`, `payload.model`). Not the reward-hacking-flagged rung. I checked the reward-hacking surface anyway, since a rename bead is the classic place to weaken a test into agreement: the pre-existing assertion `beads: { ready: 1, malformed: 1 }` became `{ open: 1, malformed: 1 }` — same strength, same arity — and two assertions were added, none removed or loosened. Clean.

Round one. **I block on nothing.**

**1. (non-blocking, infrastructure) The Warden's scratch copy cannot reproduce `verify.sh` green — and this is not caused by the diff.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:33-36` builds the scratch tree with `rsync -a --exclude '.git' --exclude '.env*' --exclude '.beads' --exclude 'bin' --exclude 'obj' --exclude 'node_modules'`. Those patterns are unanchored, so rsync matches them at every depth:
- `--exclude '.beads'` strips `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` (present in the worktree, absent in `/tmp/warden-oc8`). Result: 3 of 17 tests fail in every Warden review — 2 in `test/status.test.ts`, 1 in `test/world.test.ts` — all with `beads: null`, all unrelated to whatever is under review.
- `--exclude 'bin'` strips the repo's own `bin/` (`fort-init`, `regent`, `civ-index`), which `verify.sh`'s final step shellchecks by name. That step can never run its full surface here.

The intent is obviously to exclude the fort's *own* `.beads` database and .NET-style build output; the fix is to anchor the patterns (`--exclude '/.beads'`, `--exclude '/bin'`, `--exclude '/obj'`). Threat model: **agent accident (#1)**. A reviewer that cannot reproduce the verifier either learns to wave red output through or blocks on noise, and both failure modes degrade the only judgment gate in the merge flow. `warden.sh` is a launcher, so this is human gate 1 — it lands as a bead applied by the Overseer's hand, never by a seat. The bead should also **audit whether earlier verdicts claiming a green verifier were actually reproduced in a scratch copy or taken from Forge's report**: the fixture (`0807f41`) predates the Warden launcher (`8897c75`), and `fortkit-jmq` round 2 was recorded as "verifier green" on 2026-08-04. I am flagging that as a question to answer, not asserting the record is false — I do not have those transcripts.

**2. (non-blocking) `expect(worldPage).not.toContain("ready")` bans a substring across the whole page, not just the label.** It will also reject legitimate future strings that happen to contain it — `document.readyState`, the word "already" in a title or comment. It fails loudly and safely and is trivially fixed when it fires, and the breadth is arguably the point for this bead, so I would not change it under protest. Narrowing it to the label expression (as the sibling assertion already does) would keep the guarantee without the false-positive surface.

**3. (non-blocking) The handoff names the model imprecisely.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md:2` says "GPT-5.6 Codex"; the event stream says `gpt-5.6-terra`. The charter requires every bead and handoff to record which model did the work, and the Warden weights scrutiny by rung — "GPT-5.6 Codex" does not distinguish Terra from Sol, and Sol carries the reward-hacking flag in `fort/seats/warden.md:10`. Name the rung as the events do. Same file, minor: the header timestamp `T12:15:00-08:00` postdates its own commit (`a6104ec`, 12:13:07).

**4. (non-blocking) The Overseer's routing instruction is recorded where it will not be found.** The 2026-08-07 ruling says true `ready` "becomes computable only if the export carries dependency edges (verify during bzx decomposition)" — but `fortkit-bzx` carries no note of that obligation; it lives only in a comment on this bead, which is about to close. Cheap Mayor fix: put it on `bzx`.

**5. (non-blocking, and the reason this is APPROVE and not ESCALATE) Human gate 1's wording is broader than its mechanical enforcement, and a future Warden will have to re-derive that.** The charter says the constitution is "`fort/` files, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles". Read literally, the added `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md` is a `fort/` file and this review is a mandatory escalation. Read against the kernel mask (`fort/remember.md:17`: `.claude/`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/` are read-only to every seat) and against the charter's own Memory section, which designates `fort/handoffs/` as expected seat output, a Forge handoff is routine operation and escalating on it is ceremony. I have taken the second reading. An amendment bead narrowing gate 1's prose to match what the mask actually enforces would save every future Warden this derivation — and this diff touches no charter, seat file, profile, or launcher.

**6. (non-blocking, recorded, no action) The `/world` JSON shape change is breaking for any external consumer.** I grepped the repository: `WorldFort` and the `/world` endpoint have exactly one consumer, the page embedded in `src/server.ts`, shipped from the same build. No Herald, digest, or `civ/` reader touches it. That there is no consumer yet is precisely why the Overseer ruled this lands first, and the window closes the moment a fort enables JSONL export.

**Verified independently, in this session, in `/tmp/warden-oc8`:**
- The full diff, diffstat, and both commit hashes; `2a96ef48ce5e5ac2799ef4c0c1b8c4970fa1630e` matches the handoff's claim exactly.
- `src/readers/beads.ts`: `counts.open` is incremented only for records whose `status` string is literally `"open"`, via the `statuses` map. The new label is therefore true, and no status maps to `ready` — confirming the bead's premise.

- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`: TypeScript typecheck clean; Biome clean (32 files); ShellCheck clean on every script present in the scratch copy; Vitest **14 passed / 3 failed**, with all 3 failures traced to finding 1.
- The new assertions in isolation: `npx vitest run test/world.test.ts -t "self-contained polling page"` — **1 passed**. This is the bead's actual deliverable and it passed under my own hand.
- The 3 failures are not the diff. I read the excluded fixture in the worktree and hand-evaluated the reader against it: records `a`/`b`/`c`/`d`/`not json` yield open 1, inProgress 1, blocked 1, closed 1, malformed 1 — exactly the two failing assertions' expectations (`{blocked:1,closed:1,inProgress:1,malformed:1,open:1}` and `{open:1,malformed:1}`). The diff does not touch `test/fixtures/`.
- Model rung, and that the two prior review attempts recorded `incident` + `session.end` with `verdict_recorded:false` — the launcher behaved correctly and the bead comment's account of it is accurate.

**Taken on faith:** Forge's claim that `verify.sh --no-emit` passed 17/17 in the worktree. I cannot run it there without writing to a tree I have no business writing to. It is corroborated as far as it can be: I reproduced 14 of those 17 and hand-executed the reader over the real fixture for the other 3. I also take on faith the original intent behind `warden.sh`'s exclude list, and that no unversioned local consumer reads the `/world` JSON.

Findings 1-5 are beads, not blockers. Merge may proceed.

title: forge.sh: no concurrency guard or liveness record — two launchers can work the same bead in one worktree
description:
Incident 2026-08-04: the Mayor's harness session died during Kethra's first fortkit-gzn run; on resume the Mayor assumed the launcher process was dead (it was not), emitted a false session.end at 09:54:16, and launched a second forge.sh on the same bead. Both codex sessions ran concurrently in /home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/gzn from 09:54:22 until the first completed at 09:58:14; the duplicate was TaskStop'd and corrections appended to the stream.

Two missing mechanisms: (1) forge.sh takes no lock — nothing prevents two launchers on the same bead/worktree (flock on the worktree or a pidfile lease; second launcher refuses or adopts). (2) The launcher records no PID/liveness anywhere, so a resuming harness cannot check whether a session is alive and must guess. The charter's failover clause ('lease expiry returns the bead to ready') presumes leases that do not exist yet.

Same launcher ships in templates/fort/scripts/, so every fort inherits the race. Fix live + template together or coordinate with fortkit-ebm's template pass.
design: Sketch: flock -n on $wt/.forge.lock held for the session; write {pid, bead, model, started} to the lockfile; second invocation exits loudly with the holder's info. Liveness = kill -0 $pid. Lease expiry (charter failover) = lock released on process death, which flock gives for free.

title: Two calendars: beads stores UTC, the event stream stores local time and local-dated filenames
description: The two sources the viewer joins disagree about what day it is. Evidence, same act, 2026-08-03 evening: bd show b37 --json reports created_at 2026-08-04T07:23:59Z; the event emitted for the same work reads 2026-08-03T23:24:56-08:00. fort/scripts/emit.sh additionally names its file by LOCAL date (events-$(date +%F).jsonl), so any work after 16:00 local (UTC midnight, PST) lands in an event file dated one day before the beads that record it. Consequences: (1) a replay of founding day (fortkit-dtn) shows beads created on a day the stream says has not happened; (2) the world view will sort forts by founding date inconsistently across sources; (3) every fort in the civilization founded in the evening inherits the split, since fort-init ships emit.sh. Fix is NOT to rewrite the stream (append-only, standing order 7): readers normalize to one basis at read time, and schema/events.md states explicitly which basis each source uses and which is canonical. Decide the canonical basis before fortkit-jmq builds the readers, so this is designed in rather than retrofitted. Found 2026-08-03 by Emrith Cairnwright while verifying bead state after the Founding Moot.
design: RECOMMENDATION (Emrith, for approval, not applied): canonical instant basis is UTC; local time is a display concern only. Note that no data is actually wrong today — every event ts carries an explicit offset, so its instant is unambiguous, and beads UTC is unambiguous. The only ambiguous artifact is the FILENAME, which is a local-date shard. Therefore the cheapest correct fix needs no rewrite and no change to emitted records: (1) readers parse the offset and group by UTC, never by filename; (2) schema/events.md states that events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl is a shard key and not a fact, and that any day-grouping (digest, replay scrubber, world-view founding dates) is computed from parsed timestamps; (3) a reader test asserts that an event written at 23:24-08:00 is grouped with beads created at 07:23Z the next calendar day. Leaves emit.sh untouched, keeps the stream append-only, and costs one sentence in the schema plus one test. Requires the Overseer's or the Warden's nod before it becomes schema law, since other settlements vendor this file.
close_reason: DECIDED as recommended, verbatim: readers group by parsed UTC and never by filename; schema/events.md (canonical) and our vendored copy now declare the day-file a shard key, not a fact; the 23:24-08:00/07:24Z pinning test is a required deliverable of the maiden readers (fortkit-jmq, now unblocked). emit.sh untouched; stream append-only; elder forts' vendored copies follow via fortkit-nd6.
